what: J8 — the chunk concatenation learns a second codec. `renderChunked` opened its one video track with `pickEncodingTarget`'s codec ('avc') while `render.ts` had encoded the chunks with AV1 under O9(b)'s `?colour=all`, so the whole chunked path declined at 4:4:4 and every edit re-rendered the whole take. The track is now opened from the FIRST CHUNK'S OWN TRACK, and a set whose chunks disagree on codec family, codec string or decoder description is refused rather than muxed.
how: node scripts/exp.mjs j5 '{"takeSec":30,"quietMs":60000}' --query=colour=all (J5's own rig, the DONE gate) and node scripts/exp.mjs chunkrender '{"takeSec":30}' [--query=colour=all|cq=off] (J1's own rig, which compares the chunked lane against the unbroken one). Both through scripts/gate.sh, 2026-09-05, same machine, same hour. The J1 rig grew two facts for this task: the output file's CODEC STRING, and whether a real decoder takes its first frame — every packet count it reports is read `metadataOnly`, which never touches a decoder and would believe a wrong av1C as readily as a right one.
headline: THE EDIT LOOP AT 4:4:4 IS NOW THE EDIT LOOP AT 4:2:0: a second small edit re-renders 3 chunks of 12 and reuses 9, in 4446.6 ms, where before J8 it re-rendered the whole take in 9533.9 ms with nothing reused. The concatenated file is the same codec the unbroken render produces (av01.1.08M.08.0.110.06.06.06.0, AV1 profile 1), the same 900 packets at the same 12 keyframes at identical timestamps, and a decoder takes its first frame. The 4:2:0 path is unmoved: same codec, same 900/12, 0 % size delta, and the two lanes still come out PIXEL-IDENTICAL.

unit.gate: the two refusal rules are born red
unit.result: src/core/compose/chunkedCodec.test.ts — 10 tests. With the codec-family and codec-string tests removed from `sameTrack`, 2 of them fail; restored, 10 pass. Full suite 1406 passed, typecheck clean.

the_one_thing_that_is_not_free.finding: At 4:4:4 the chunked file is 19.5 % SMALLER than the unbroken one on the same 900 packets, and the two are 99 / 37.1 / 51.8 dB apart at 1.5 / 15 / 27 s. At 4:2:0 they are pixel-identical.
the_one_thing_that_is_not_free.it_is_not_the_concatenation: MEASURED, not argued. Run the SAME 4:2:0 lanes with constant quality off (--query=cq=off) and AVC diverges the same way: 99 / 40.6 / 49.1 dB, size -3 %. So this is what a BITRATE-TARGETED encoder does when its rate control runs over twelve 2.5 s segments instead of one 30 s stream — it has been true of J1's chunked path on the AVC rung since J1 shipped, for anyone who turns `?cq=` off.
the_one_thing_that_is_not_free.why_444_meets_it: `constantQualityCodec` returns null for anything that is not avc (render.ts), so the 4:4:4 rung carries no quality string and is bitrate-targeted. Constant quality — the shipped default, qp 20 — pins the QP and is exactly why the 4:2:0 lanes come out identical.
the_one_thing_that_is_not_free.what_it_is_not: It is not a colour loss: 4:4:4 stores chroma per pixel either way. It is a different bit budget, and the chunked lane spent fewer bits.
the_one_thing_that_is_not_free.what_it_would_take: A quality target for the AV1 rung, the way `?cq=` gives one to AVC. That is a task, not this one, and it is worth having BEFORE any 4:4:4 default moves.

verdict: J8 IS DONE. The concatenation reads the codec off the chunks, a mixed set is refused rather than mis-muxed, and the j5 rig at --query=colour=all reports 3 of 12 re-rendered and 9 reused — the number it reports at 4:2:0. The colour default is now a question about Robert's eye and about the bit-budget note above, and nothing else.
